batch_strategy: matched condition and loading contrasts with upper-tail repair and undercovered graph exploration

choices.reason: m123 at 5/1 provides a condition label on a sparsely supervised ether-rich aromatic graph. Its predicted V2 interval is broad enough to test whether the model transfers response information from more common methoxy and ester environments.

m182 at 20/1 has high CW distance and a wide predicted V1/V2 interval. It is one point in a fixed-loading m182 curve with the selected 0/1 and 2/1 rows, allowing endpoint-specific solvent-response learning.

m56 at 20/1 and 50 ul with PE/200 can be compared directly with the selected m56 10/1 row. The matched loading contrast tests whether its response is smooth and whether onset and finish shift together.

m202 at 10/1 has high CW distance and a broad V2 prediction. This charged phosphorus-containing graph is an undercovered structural environment where direct supervision can reveal a representation gap.

m182 at 2/1 and the same 150 ul DCM/300 ul loading as the selected 0/1 and 20/1 rows completes a controlled three-point response curve. It is especially useful for distinguishing gradual growth from a localized transition.

m182 at 0/1 supplies the weakest-eluent anchor for the fixed-loading curve. Together with the two selected stronger conditions, it teaches the two endpoint heads the direction and curvature of the response.

m9 at 50/1 samples a high-ratio condition on a nonpolar brominated biphenyl graph. The label tests whether the model's high-ratio correction transfers to a graph with no hydrogen-bond donors or acceptors.
m167 at 5/1 probes a fluorinated diketone environment with a relatively wide predicted finish interval. It supplies carbonyl-rich upper-tail supervision distinct from the acetoacetate observations.

m129 at 2/1 has high CW distance and a broad V2 prediction. The thioether-substituted benzaldehyde tests whether sulfur-containing carbonyl graphs receive inappropriate response transfer from oxygen-only analogues.
m121 at 50/1 samples a high-ratio methoxy aryl halide with a wide finish interval. It can improve calibration for late conditions in a graph lacking a carbonyl or donor.

m209 at 1/1 provides a low-strength phenolic anchor in a family where measured phenolic curves have not shared one universal response shape. It helps test how much of the correction is scaffold-specific.

m56 at 10/1 is the matched lower-ratio companion to the selected m56 20/1 row, with the same PE loading conditions. Their difference can supervise a local solvent-response slope without conflating amount.
m122 at 2/1 probes a dibromo methoxy aromatic graph with a moderately broad V2 prediction. This is useful for testing halogenated aromatic transfer separately from the simpler m121 condition.
m208 at 5/1 targets an iodophenol graph at high loading-solvent volume and moderate CW distance. It extends the phenolic evidence into a different substitution and amount regime.

m94 at 0/1 is a low-strength anchor for a cyclopropyl diketone graph whose predicted V2 interval is wider than its onset interval. It can establish a baseline before stronger-condition transfer is learned.
m49 at 50/1 probes a bulky dialkyl benzaldehyde at a high ratio and high CW distance. The label can reveal whether steric substitution changes the late finish relative to simpler aromatic aldehydes.

m186 at 2/1 samples a brominated hydroxybenzaldehyde environment with a wide predicted interval. It provides a direct structural comparison to the measured salicylaldehyde and bromosalicylaldehyde responses.

m25 at 10/1 bridges the measured m25 5/1 and 20/1 conditions, including b6017da51a674177d16d and 0af9d219be9872711215. This interior point can distinguish gradual finish growth from a sharp transition in an acetoacetate ester.
m179 at 5/1 adds a cyclic ketone graph with a moderate predicted V2 width to the carbonyl response set. It tests transfer from open-chain ketones without duplicating the acetoacetate family.

m58 at 2/1 samples a phenolic alcohol graph with a broad predicted finish interval. It helps determine whether the phenolic response behavior seen in m197, m190 and m209 transfers to a noncarbonyl alcohol.
m151 at 2/1 and 100 ul provides one member of a matched amount contrast with the selected 50 ul m151 row. Holding ratio, solvent and loading-solvent volume fixed isolates a sample-amount effect.

m101 at 20/1 and reduced recorded sample volume is a high-CW amount-response experiment. It can test whether the loading association learned from m125 and m135 transfers to a halogenated aromatic ester.
m120 at 2/1 has a broad predicted interval on an oxygenated aromatic graph. It expands loading and condition coverage beyond the already measured methoxy aldehyde and alcohol examples.

m104 at 2/1 provides a condition label for an aminobenzoate graph with very low CW distance but a nontrivial predicted finish interval. It can improve local interpolation around an H-bond-donor-containing ester.

m27 at 1/1 supplies a lower-strength baseline for the measured m27 sequence. The observed m27 rows 8748c66e5f0823e6a65, c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc and a3c1a0ac40733e8650fb show an unexpectedly shallow and short response, so this label tests the lower boundary without assuming renewed growth.

m109 at 20/1 probes a methoxy bromofluoro aromatic graph at a condition where its predicted finish interval is moderately wide. It tests halogen and anisole response transfer separately from carbonyl-rich rows.

m202 at 0/1 supplies the low-strength companion to the selected 5/1 and 10/1 m202 rows. Although the recorded amount differs, the three labels provide useful response-shape supervision for this charged phosphorus graph.
m151 at 2/1 and 50 ul is the lower-amount companion to the selected 100 ul m151 row. The matched pair isolates sample amount while retaining the same mobile phase and loading-solvent volume.
m202 at 5/1 adds an interior condition point between the selected 0/1 and 10/1 rows. It can distinguish a smooth response from a ratio-specific jump in the undercovered charged graph.
m188 at 20/1 has high CW distance and a broad predicted V2 interval. This halogenated benzaldehyde graph tests upper-tail transfer from the measured aldehyde and phenolic families.

m97 at 1/1 gives a low-strength label for a brominated ester graph with high molecule novelty relative to nearby condition-response examples. It supports structural interpolation across aromatic ester substitutions.

m101 at 20/1 and higher recorded volume completes an amount contrast with the selected lower-volume m101 row. The pair can determine whether amount changes mainly onset, finish, or both at this ratio.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response curves are scaffold-specific, and V1 and V2 can change on different scales; broad finish growth should be learned from matched condition curves rather than imposed as a universal correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched local curves teach the two endpoint heads whether solvent strength moves onset, finish, or both, improving generalization across condition ratios.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m182, m202, m56 and m27 points show smooth response, a localized transition, or separate V1 and V2 regimes?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading context affect retention in scaffold- and ratio-dependent ways, with the strongest effects often appearing in V1 or V2 separately.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m151 and m101 matched amount contrasts can repair weak loading dependence and show whether amount effects transfer across chemical families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: When ratio and loading solvent are fixed, do the selected amount pairs shift V1, V2, or both, and is the direction family-specific?

hypotheses.content: Upper-tail V2 calibration remains weak in several polar, oxygen-rich and carbonyl-rich families, even when the corresponding onset is reasonably predicted.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Broad-tail labels can improve V2 calibration and prevent the model from transferring late finishes indiscriminately across polar and carbonyl-rich structures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which selected high-width rows produce genuine late finishes, and which reveal over-dispersed or misplaced model tails?

hypotheses.content: Undercovered charged, phosphorus-containing, phenolic, halogenated and sulfur-containing graph environments require direct structure-condition labels because descriptor and fingerprint similarity may transfer endpoint curves poorly.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct labels on chemically unusual graphs can expose representation gaps that nearest-neighbor transfer and broad solvent corrections will miss.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m202, m182, m209, m129 and m188 experiments share a transferable response pattern or require separate graph-specific corrections?

feedback_interpretation: The recent aminobenzonitrile measurements confirmed steep 2/1-to-5/1 growth, while amount transfer was close for m160 but shifted onset more for m161. The m95 interior measurements supported finish growth rather than the earlier predicted valley. m27 at 20/1 remained unusually early, so I am treating its response as scaffold-specific. The m125 results strengthened the ratio-dependent loading hypothesis, and the phenolic measurements weakened a shared response-valley explanation. This batch therefore emphasizes fixed-loading curves for m182, m56 and m202, matched amount contrasts for m151 and m101, and broad-tail supervision across structurally different graphs.
batch_rationale: The 32 labels form several interpretable local experiments. The m182 and m202 groups provide multi-ratio curves on undercovered graphs; m56 supplies a fixed-loading PE response contrast; m151 and m101 isolate amount effects at fixed ratio and loading solvent. Additional phenolic, halogenated, sulfur-containing, ester and carbonyl rows repair structural transfer and V2 upper-tail behavior. The batch uses observed response patterns such as the m95 finish expansion, the m27 shallow response, the m125 loading associations and the divergent phenolic curves to guide selection, while treating candidate widths and CW distances as model behavior rather than measured error. These labels should improve separate V1/V2 response learning, loading dependence, structural transfer and upper-tail calibration across the Row-distribution.
